title: Multiply Strings
description:
Given two non-negative integers `num1` and `num2` represented as strings of decimal digits, return their product, also as a string.

You may not convert the whole strings to integers with a built-in parser or use big-integer libraries; work with the digits.

examples.explanation: No leading zeros in the result.

constraints: Digits only, no leading zeros except the number 0 itself.
hints: Long multiplication: the digit at position i of num1 times the digit at position j of num2 contributes to position i + j of the result (counting from the least significant end).
Allocate an integer array of length len(num1) + len(num2), accumulate every digit product into its slot, then do one pass to propagate carries.
Strip leading zeros at the end, but keep a single 0 if the product is zero.
signature: def multiply(self, num1: str, num2: str) -> str:
approach:
**Key insight: in long multiplication, the product of the digit at power `10^i` and the digit at power `10^j` lands at power `10^(i+j)`. Accumulate all of those partial products into an array indexed by power, then fix up carries in one pass.**

Reverse both strings so index equals power of ten. For every pair `(i, j)` add `a[i] * b[j]` into `slots[i + j]`. The slots temporarily hold values larger than 9, which is fine in Python (in fixed-width languages the maximum is `81 * 200 + carry`, still tiny). Then sweep from the lowest power upward, keeping `total % 10` and carrying `total // 10`. Finally strip high-order zeros and reverse back into a string.

**Why it is correct:** the product of the two numbers is the double sum of `a[i] * b[j] * 10^(i+j)`, which is exactly what the slot array represents before normalisation; the carry pass converts that representation to canonical base-10 digits without changing the value. The result has at most `m + n` digits, so the array never overflows.

**Common mistakes:** doing carries inside the double loop (correct but fiddly and error-prone); forgetting the zero case and returning `"000"`; building the result with string concatenation from the front (quadratic); using `int(num1) * int(num2)`, which an interviewer will reject.

**Interview follow-ups:** (1) Add two numeric strings (Add Strings, the carry pass alone). (2) Karatsuba multiplication for `O(n^1.585)`, and when it is worth it. (3) Negative numbers and a decimal point: strip the sign and the point, multiply, then reinsert.
